title: Blogger Operators & Expressions Master Catalog
description: Canonical machine-readable catalog of Blogger expression operators, dual-syntax execution grammar, 11-level precedence hierarchy, operand typing, and compiler quotas.

precedence_hierarchy.category: Arithmetic (Additive), URL, Date, Image & Snippet Transforms

compiler_quotas.token_cost_rules: 1 token per operator (2 for ternary ? :), 1 per literal/operand (including unary negative numbers), 1 per data path (including static and dynamic bracket indexing), 1 per array/object container, 1 per grouping parentheses pair ( ... ), 0 for argument parentheses in function calls/lambdas, and 0 for object property keys and delimiters (, and :)

js_methods.description: JavaScript method calls are invalid in Blogger expressions. Use native operators and helpers.

js_equality_operators.description: Strict equality (===, !==) is not supported in Blogger expressions; use == or !=.

concatenation.name: Concatenation
concatenation.description: String concatenation and scalar text interpolation.

arithmetic.name: Arithmetic
arithmetic.description: Numeric addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulo.

comparison.name: Comparison
comparison.description: Relational comparisons and value equality checks.

logical.name: Logical
logical.description: Logical conjunction, disjunction, and boolean inversion.

membership.name: Membership
membership.description: Tests whether an item exists within a collection or string.

content.name: Content
content.description: Substring search and item containment checks.

collection.name: Collection
collection.description: Array slicing, pagination limits, and numeric sequence generation.

lambda.name: Lambda / Collection Pipeline
lambda.description: Higher-order collection predicates, projection mapping, and aggregation reductions.

ternary.name: Ternary / Conditional
ternary.description: Inline conditional branching expression (cond ? val1 : val2).

elvis.name: Coalescence / Fallback
elvis.description: Primary nullish fallback value selector for null or undeclared operands (?:).

url.name: Transform / URL
url.description: URL path segment joining, query parameter appending, and hash fragmenting.

date.name: Transform / Date
date.description: Localized date formatting using ICU pattern tokens.

image.name: Transform / Image
image.description: Google CDN image thumbnail resizing and responsive srcset generation.

snippet.name: Transform / Truncation
snippet.description: Text truncation, snippet extraction, and HTML tag stripping.

+.description: Performs numeric addition on numbers or string concatenation when at least one operand is text (ad-hoc polymorphism).

overloads.description: Arithmetic addition on numbers or skin dimension lengths
String concatenation and scalar text interpolation
String concatenation when right operand is text

-.description: Performs arithmetic subtraction on numbers/lengths or unary negation on numeric literals (e.g. -5).
anti_patterns: Unary negation cannot be applied to parenthesized compound expressions like '-(a - b)'; unary minus is strictly supported only on immediate numeric literals like -5.

/.description: Division of numbers rendered with up to 4 decimal places.
anti_patterns: Division by zero aborts expression evaluation.
Modulo by zero aborts expression evaluation.

==.description: Value equality test. Employs canonical scalar string coercion: numbers coerce to canonical string format (e.g. 0 == "0" is true, but 0 == "00" is false), booleans coerce to "true"/"false" strings (e.g. true == "true" is true, but true == 1 is false). Missing/undefined properties equal empty string "", while empty arrays do not coerce to false, 0, or empty string. Objects and Date instances are compared by identity.
anti_patterns: Do not use JavaScript '===' triple equals in Blogger expressions.
Do not expect boolean-to-number coercion (e.g. true == 1 evaluates to false).

!=.description: Value inequality test. Evaluates to the logical inversion of == using identical canonical coercion rules.
anti_patterns: Do not use JavaScript '!==' in Blogger expressions.

<.description: Less than relational comparison. Operands are strictly restricted to scalar numbers. Strings and unformatted Date objects cannot be compared directly with relational operators and abort with a compiler error; use numeric Date modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric comparisons instead.
anti_patterns: Do not compare strings or Date objects directly with relational operators (e.g. data:post.date < data:post.date); use numeric modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric values.

>.description: Greater than relational comparison. Operands are strictly restricted to scalar numbers. Strings and unformatted Date objects cannot be compared directly with relational operators and abort with a compiler error; use numeric Date modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric comparisons instead.
anti_patterns: Do not compare strings or Date objects directly with relational operators (e.g. data:post.date > data:post.date); use numeric modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric values.

<=.description: Less than or equal relational comparison. Operands are strictly restricted to scalar numbers. Strings and unformatted Date objects cannot be compared directly with relational operators and abort with a compiler error; use numeric Date modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric comparisons instead.
anti_patterns: Do not compare strings or Date objects directly with relational operators (e.g. data:post.date <= data:post.date); use numeric modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric values.

>=.description: Greater than or equal relational comparison. Operands are strictly restricted to scalar numbers. Strings and unformatted Date objects cannot be compared directly with relational operators and abort with a compiler error; use numeric Date modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric comparisons instead.
anti_patterns: Do not compare strings or Date objects directly with relational operators (e.g. data:post.date >= data:post.date); use numeric modifiers (.year, .month, .day, .dayOfYear) or numeric values.

and.description: Logical conjunction returning true if both operands are truthy.
anti_patterns: Avoid JavaScript '&&' in XML attributes to prevent XML entity escaping collisions; prefer keyword 'and'.

or.description: Logical disjunction returning true if either operand is truthy.
anti_patterns: Avoid JavaScript '||' in expressions; prefer keyword 'or' or elvis '?:'.

in.description: Tests whether an element exists within an array or character sequence within a string. Evaluates using canonical equality coercion across collection elements (e.g. "2" in [1, 2, 3] and false in ["false", "true"] evaluate to true; empty string "" is always in string).

overloads.description: Array membership check with canonical equality coercion
Substring membership check in character sequence

contains.description: Tests whether a string contains a substring or an array contains an item (haystack contains needle). Evaluates using canonical equality coercion across collection elements (e.g. [1, 2, 3] contains "2" evaluates to true; string substring search is case-sensitive, and "" is always contained).

overloads.description: Substring containment check within parent string
Array item containment check with canonical equality coercion

anti_patterns: Do not use JavaScript .includes() or .indexOf(); use keyword operator 'contains'.

not in.description: Negated membership test; returns true if item is absent from collection or substring is absent from parent string.

not contains.description: Negated containment test; returns true if container does not contain element or substring.

take.description: Extracts up to N items from the beginning of an array.

operands.name: count
operands.description: Maximum number of items to take

anti_patterns: Do not use JavaScript .slice() to limit collections; use 'take' or 'limit'.

skip.description: Bypasses the first N items of an array and returns the remaining elements.

operands.name: count
operands.description: Number of leading items to skip

to.description: Generates an array sequence of integers between two integer bounds (inclusive). Exclusive to <b:loop values='...'>.
anti_patterns: 'to' is valid exclusively within <b:loop values='...'>; using 'to' in cond or b:eval is invalid.

any.description: Quantifier returning true if at least one item satisfies the arrow predicate.
anti_patterns: Do not prefix iterator properties with 'data:' inside the lambda body (e.g. p.title, never data:p.title).

all.description: Quantifier returning true if every element in the collection satisfies the arrow predicate.

none.description: Quantifier returning true if zero items in the collection satisfy the arrow predicate.

count.description: Counts the number of elements in a collection that satisfy the arrow predicate.

map.description: Projects each element into a new transformed array using the lambda expression.
anti_patterns: Do not use JavaScript .map() method; use keyword operator: array map (p => ...)

filter.description: Filters an array keeping only elements satisfying the boolean predicate.
anti_patterns: Do not use JavaScript .filter() method; use keyword operator: array filter (p => ...)

first.description: Extracts the first element satisfying the predicate, or null if none match.

?:.description: Primary nullish coalescence operator. Returns fallback value if left operand evaluates to null or missing/undefined data (note: non-null values such as empty strings '', numeric zero 0, boolean false, and empty arrays [] do not trigger the fallback).

operands.name: target
operands.description: Value to inspect for null or undeclared state

? :.description: Inline conditional branching expression (condition ? truthyValue : falsyValue).
anti_patterns: Concatenation '+' binds tighter than ternary; always wrap ternary in parentheses when concatenating.

path.description: Replaces the pathname portion of a URL (ensuring a single leading '/') while preserving origin, existing query parameters, and hash fragments.

params.description: Sets or replaces the entire query string on a URL using key-value pairs from a dictionary object, deterministically serializing parameters in alphabetical key order (?k1=v1&k2=v2).
anti_patterns: Mandatory whitespace after colons in object literals { key: value } to avoid namespace collisions.

appendParams.description: Merges and appends additional query parameters from a dictionary object onto a URL while preserving existing query parameters.

fragment.description: Appends or replaces the anchor/hash fragment identifier (#anchor) of a URL.

format.description: Formats a timestamp date value using an ICU date-time format pattern string, automatically applying the blog's configured locale.

resizeImage.description: Rewrites Google CDN image URLs for resizing (w<size>), aspect ratio cropping (w<width>-h<height>-p-k-no-nu), or responsive variant collections. Scalar resize returns an image descriptor that serializes to the resized URL in scalar output contexts and populates .width and .height modifiers. Array resize returns array[object] of image_variant items with .url and .size. When evaluated against non-Google CDN URLs, safely returns the original URL unmodified without compiler diagnostics.

operands.name: size
operands.description: Target dimension or array of dimensions

overloads.description: Scalar image resize returning a resized image URL descriptor with populated .width and .height modifiers.
Array of responsive image_variant objects with .url and .size properties.

anti_patterns: Only works on Google-hosted image infrastructure; guard with .isResizable modifier.
Do not pass the result of resizeImage(...) as the first argument to sourceSet(...); pass the raw source image URL directly to sourceSet.

sourceSet.description: Generates a comma-separated HTML srcset string formatted as '<resized_url> <size>w, ...' from a raw Google CDN image URL and an array of integer width dimensions.

operands.name: image
operands.description: Raw source Google CDN image URL (not a resizeImage result)

anti_patterns: The first argument to sourceSet(image, sizes[, ratio]) must be a raw image URL or image reference (e.g. data:post.featuredImage), never the result of resizeImage(...).

snippet.description: Extracts a truncated plain-text snippet from markup or text, stripping HTML tags and appending a horizontal ellipsis character ('…') when truncated (unless ellipsis: false is specified in options).

operands.name: options
operands.description: Snippet options: length (number), links (boolean), linebreaks (boolean), ellipsis (boolean)

anti_patterns: Whitespace required after colon in options dictionary: { length: 150, links: false }.
